Scope: infrastructure over about 6.5 km² of the Fourth Industrial City in Riyadh: roads and tunnels, electrical, telecom, ICT and security networks, potable water and fire-fighting, irrigation, sewage and stormwater networks, and sewage and stormwater pumping stations.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 25.2% against 30.1% planned, the project is behind by 4.9% (SPI 0.84). It gained 1.6% this week against 0.8% planned, so the gap narrowed from 5.8% last week. Earthworks remain far ahead of plan, but procurement, the zone network works and the tunnels are behind.

The schedule still finishes the project about eight months late. The P6 extract in this week's report finishes the project on 01-Feb-2029, 247 days after the contract completion date of 30-May-2028 (last week: 13-Feb-2029, −259 days). The report's General Information sheet still gives 06-Feb-2029. The "Complete MV and road works" milestone (30-Sep-2026) has passed with asphalt at 11.0% and the MV network at 0.3% installed.

Earthworks and wet networks movingCut is 86.0% and fill 90.6% complete. Subgrade reached 50.0% and asphalt 11.0% (+2,555 m³ this week); aggregate base course stayed at 22.6%. The storm network rose to 69.2% (+4,244 m) and sewage to 60.5% (+2,188 m).

Open issues and risks

IssueOwnerDetail
Clash with SEC high-voltage cablesContractor / SECHigh-voltage cables of the Saudi Electricity transmission company clash with Road C2. A technical solution was submitted and is awaiting SEC's reply. Rated critical; target 30-Oct-2026.
Clash with SEC medium-voltage cablesContractor / SECMV cables clash with Road C8. SEC's contractor (Pillar) has visited the site and a start-of-work record was signed. Rated critical.
Clash with Green Riyadh servicesContractor / Green RiyadhAn air vent and cathodic protection on Road C8 clash with the works. Coordination with Green Riyadh's contractor is ongoing to get drawings and price the diversion. Rated critical.
Clash with ARAMCO gas linesContractor / ARAMCOWet and dry networks on Roads C8 and RD-L10 clash with two ARAMCO gas lines. Technical solutions were submitted and await ARAMCO's reply; solutions for telecom, sewage, MV, ICT and LV are already approved. Rated high.
Procurement delaysContractorPurchase orders had to be revised after the design changes, and material prices rose. Orders are now issued and supply is under way. Rated high.
Progress behind planContractorProgress lags the schedule because of the master plan change (Wadi Al-Sulai) and the equipment shortage at the start. Most shop drawings are done and equipment and network crews were increased. Rated critical.

Delay reasons stated in the report: the master layout changed after the Wadi Al-Sulai redesign, which changed the design of all networks; and equipment was short at the start of the project.

Data notes

This report uses the weekly report uploaded for 26-Oct-2026 and, for this-week values, the 19-Oct-2026 report. Every progress percentage is physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. There is no S-curve section: the workbook's Physical-Chart Data sheet is empty.

  • The week number, 47, is the contract week stated on the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 47 of 130").
  • The workbook also gives a cost-based progress figure, labelled as actual progress in places. This report does not use it.
  • Three completion dates appear in the workbook: 30-May-2028 (Milestones sheet), 06-Feb-2029 (General Information, not updated since last week) and 01-Feb-2029 (P6 extract, −247 days float; last week 13-Feb-2029).
  • Procurement man-hour progress is only 6.6%, although 87–99% of the wet-network pipes are delivered. This week the Major Quantities sheet was updated to show the deliveries; last week it showed 1–3%.
  • The safety statistics (18,000 man-hours this week, 458,560 cumulative) and the quality counts are identical to last week's report, so they appear not to have been updated.
  • The October manual head count was changed from 252 (last week's report) to 249.
  • The revised BOQ total changed from 374,123,662 to 352,632,896 SAR with no explanation.
  • Invoices: the workbook lists 8 invoices, 71,001,361 SAR gross and none paid; last week's presentation showed 54,980,525 SAR invoiced and 41,804,647 SAR paid. The contract value of 445,000,000 SAR is called "including VAT" on the Conclusion sheet but "excluding VAT" in the bill breakdown.
  • Scope totals differ between sheets: MV 131,104 m vs 171,170 m (Major sheet); interlock 42,347 m² vs 46,105 m². Several summary panels still show #REF! or #DIV/0! errors.
  • No progress presentation or P6 update (XER) was uploaded this week. Milestone status therefore comes from the workbook only, and P6 milestone floats are not shown.
  • Photos: five are stamped 24-Oct-2026; the storm pipe photo has no stamp. A tunnel wing-wall photo dated 28-Oct-2026 (after the data date) and a second BL-31 backfilling photo were not used.
